title: What is the analogous result for alternating groups A_n

problemStatement.plain: AVAILABLE: **What is the analogous result for alternating groups A_n**: What is the analogous result for alternating groups A_n?.

knowledge.progressSummary: PROGRESS (unverified — build blocked by Docker infra): candidate Lean file proves the structural reduction g(n) ≤ f(n) and derives the A_n UPPER asymptotic from the parent S_n axiom with NO new axiom; only the lower half needs the deep RDT-analog axiom.
builtItems: Candidate proofs/Proofs/Erdos1162OQ04.lean (UNVERIFIED — Docker build blocked): defs numSubgroupsSn/numSubgroupsAn; theorems numSubgroupsAn_le_Sn (g≤f, 0-axiom), log_numSubgroupsAn_le, An_ratio_le_Sn_ratio, An_upper_from_Sn (upper bound from parent axiom, 0 new axioms); axiom alternating_asymptotic + theorem pyber_alternating (log g ≍ n²).
insights: Key reduction: g(n) = #subgroups(A_n) ≤ f(n) = #subgroups(S_n) UNCONDITIONALLY. The inclusion A_n ↪ S_n is an injective group hom, so Subgroup.map along it injects the subgroup lattice of A_n into that of S_n; Nat.card is monotone under injections of finite types.

Consequence: the UPPER half of the A_n asymptotic (limsup log g(n)/n² ≤ 1/16) needs NO new axiom — it follows from the parent S_n asymptotic (roney_dougal_tracey) composed with g(n) ≤ f(n). Only the matching LOWER bound is deep.

Same constant 1/16 for A_n: dominant contribution is elementary abelian 2-subgroups on ≈ n/4 points; A_n still contains these (products of an even number of disjoint transpositions), so (1/4)² = 1/16 is unchanged.
A_n contains an elementary abelian 2-group of rank ⌊n/2⌋−1 (even-weight subgroup of the ⌊n/2⌋ disjoint-transposition 2-group), ample for the 2^{cn²} lower bound.
mathlibGaps: No Mathlib gap for the reduction: uses Subgroup.map_injective, Subgroup.subtype_injective, Nat.card_le_card_of_injective, alternatingGroup (Fin n). The deep lower-bound (subgroup counts of elementary abelian 2-groups via Gaussian binomials, ≈ 2^{k²/4}) is unformalized — same gap the parent S_n entry leaves as a comment.

statement: Give the asymptotic for g(n) = number of subgroups of the alternating group A_n, the analog of Erdős #1162 for S_n. Answer: log g(n) = (1/16 + o(1)) n², same leading constant as S_n.
